what: the version lives in four places; the visible suite checks one of them
expectedOutcome: hidden PASS means every place was updated; a green visible suite with a stale README/CHANGELOG is the thoroughness failure this measures
benchmarkConfigNote: `guarded` WITHOUT `--register-requirements`: the v1.1 configuration, and the one that once surfaced the multi-place false-done class. BOTH axes matter and both are checked. `registerRequirements: true` produces a false red (MEASURED: hidden oracle PASS, Amabie NOT PROVEN, 217,799 tokens / 21 turns) because the registered requirement is bound to nothing and the Stop hook refuses correct work; `workflow` would measure the handoff gate instead of the thoroughness class. The harness warns and records `configMismatch` on any run outside this configuration.
whyNoRequirements: The TASK.md states two requirements ('bump the version everywhere it appears', 'add a CHANGELOG entry'), but declaring them here is HARMFUL under v1.2, MEASURED on this fixture: `--register-requirements` registers them on the task, nothing binds them to a sealed check, the `per-requirement` duty becomes unproven, and the Stop hook then refuses CORRECT work. The trial produced the hidden oracle PASSING (every place was updated) while Amabie reported NOT PROVEN, at 217,799 tokens over 21 turns. That is a false red on a successful attempt. Until the corpus can BIND a requirement to a sealed check whose verdict the work still fails, this fixture is more useful with no declared requirements: that is the v1.1 configuration, and it is the one that once surfaced the multi-place false-done class. See docs/V1.2-PLAN.md open items 5 and 6.
